subjects.blurb: Half the paper is Arithmetic + Reasoning. Your weakest area, so the biggest upside. Do the eight high-frequency topics, then volume against a clock.
47 marks and the fastest on the paper. You are already reasonable here - convert competence into speed with daily timed sets.
The single biggest General Studies topic. Finite, dense with dates, and asked every year. Aim to get almost all of it.
Learn it as ladders of dates, not as a story. The freedom struggle carries most of the marks.
Purely factual and fixed year to year. Rivers, soils, crops and states. The largest GS subject in the Mains paper.
Economy (9) plus GK and current affairs (12). Definitional, not analytical - RBI tools, revolutions, schemes and world bodies.
Pure recall - Articles, Parts, Schedules and Amendments. Index it in memory rather than understanding it deeply.
Telangana history, geography, culture and schemes outside the statehood movement. Cheap marks once the movement is done.
Physics 5.7 + Biology 5.0 + Chemistry 3.7. Do NOT study these as subjects - flashcards only. Chemistry is the lowest-yield topic in the syllabus.

tips.subject: Arithmetic
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Why this matters: "12.5% of 640" is slow. "1/8 of 640 = 80" is instant. Convert every percentage to a fraction before calculating.

tips.subject: Arithmetic
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Price rise / consumption cut: if price rises r%, consumption must fall by r/(100 + r) × 100 % to keep spending the same. Rise 25% → cut 20%.

tips.subject: Arithmetic
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Age problems: always let present ages be 5x and 7x (not x and y). One equation from the "years hence/ago" condition solves it in two lines.

tips.subject: Arithmetic
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Doubling shortcut (SI): if a sum doubles in n years, interest earned = principal, so rate = 100/n %. It becomes 3× when interest = 2P (i.e. 2n years), 4× at 3n years. Under SI these scale linearly — never do this with CI.

tips.subject: Arithmetic
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Always use the LCM units method. A does it in 12 days, B in 18 → total work = LCM(12,18) = 36 units. A = 3 units/day, B = 2 units/day. Together = 5/day → 36/5 = 7.2 days. Far faster than adding fractions. If A takes a days and B takes b days → together = ab ÷ (a + b) days M₁ × D₁ × H₁ ÷ W₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂ ÷ W₂ (men–days–hours–work) Pipes: filling = positive rate, emptying = negative rate. Add them and invert. If A is n times as efficient as B, A takes 1/n of B's time; ratio of times = inverse ratio of efficiencies

tips.subject: Arithmetic
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Late/early problems: convert the time difference to hours and set d/u − d/v = difference. "10 min late at 5 km/h, 5 min early at 6 km/h" → difference = 15 min = ¼ hr.

tips.subject: Arithmetic
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Scaling rule: if every linear dimension is multiplied by k, area is multiplied by k² and volume by k³. Radius doubled → area ×4, volume ×8.

tips.subject: Arithmetic
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Divide the exponent by 4, take the remainder, and read that position in the cycle. Remainder 0 → the last one in the cycle.

tips.subject: Arithmetic
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Questions like "(0.6³ + 0.4³) ÷ (0.6² − 0.6×0.4 + 0.4²)" are pure identity spotting — the answer is just a + b = 1. Never multiply it out.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: Trick 1 — EJOTY: instantly find any letter's position
tips.body: E = 5 · J = 10 · O = 15 · T = 20 · Y = 25 Every fifth letter. To find any letter, jump to the nearest anchor and count a step or two. R? O is 15, so P=16, Q=17, R = 18. W? T is 20, so U=21, V=22, W = 23. Never count from A again.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: Trick 2 — the opposite-letter rule
tips.body: Letter position + opposite letter position = 27 A↔Z, B↔Y, C↔X, D↔W, E↔V, F↔U, G↔T, H↔S, I↔R, J↔Q, K↔P, L↔O, M↔N. Memory sentence for the first five pairs: "AZ BY CX DW EV" — say it out loud, it rhymes. If a question asks "which letter is as far from the end as M is from the beginning", M = 13, so 27 − 13 = 14 = N. Instant.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: Common patterns worth recognising on sight
tips.body: ×2+1 · ×3−1 · +n then +(n+2) · n²−1 · n³ · prime numbers · alternating +/− If the numbers grow slowly it is an addition series; if they grow fast it is multiplication; if they grow fast and unevenly, test squares and cubes.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: Method — always draw a small tree
tips.body: Use + for male, − for female, = for married couple, a vertical line down for children, a horizontal line for siblings. Generations go in rows. Ten seconds of drawing beats a minute of confusion.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: The one rule that solves half of these
tips.body: Whenever you see "only son/daughter of my father/mother", stop and ask: is that person the speaker? In most such questions it is. Substituting "myself" immediately collapses the puzzle.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: Method
tips.body: Draw a small cross: North up, South down, East right, West left. Mark the starting point and trace each move. Do not attempt it mentally. Turning RIGHT = clockwise (N→E→S→W). Turning LEFT = anticlockwise (N→W→S→E). For a person facing south, everything reverses: their left is east and their right is west. This reversal is the single most common mistake in this topic. Shortest distance: when the path forms a right angle, use Pythagoras. 4 km north then 3 km east → √(16 + 9) = 5 km. Memorise the triplets 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 6-8-10, 8-15-17 — exam questions almost always use one of them. Rotation questions: "if south-east becomes north…" means the whole compass has turned. Work out the rotation once (here, 135° anticlockwise) and apply the same turn to the direction asked. Treat directions as angles: N = 0°, NE = 45°, E = 90°, SE = 135°, S = 180°, SW = 225°, W = 270°, NW = 315°.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Total = (rank from left) + (rank from right) − 1 Rank from right = Total − (rank from left) + 1 People between two positions = (difference of positions) − 1 Example: In a row of 25, A is 8th from the left and B is 12th from the right. How many sit between them? B from left = 25 − 12 + 1 = 14. Between = 14 − 8 − 1 = 5. Interchange trick: if two people swap places and one's new position is given, that new position is the other person's old position. Ravi 7th from left, Kiran 9th from right; after swapping Ravi is 15th from left → total = 15 + 9 − 1 = 23.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: The formula
tips.body: Angle between hands = |30H − 5.5M| where H is the hour and M the minutes. Why: the hour hand moves 30° per hour and 0.5° per minute; the minute hand moves 6° per minute. If the answer exceeds 180°, subtract it from 360°.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: The core idea
tips.body: "Odd days" are the days left over after counting complete weeks. Ordinary year = 1 odd day · Leap year = 2 odd days 100 years = 5 odd days · 200 years = 3 · 300 years = 1 · 400 years = 0 Leap year rule: divisible by 4; but a century year must be divisible by 400. So 1900 was not a leap year; 2000 was. Example: If 1 January 2024 was a Monday, what was 1 January 2025? 2024 is a leap year → 2 odd days → Monday + 2 = Wednesday. Example: If today is Wednesday, what day is it after 61 days? 61 ÷ 7 leaves remainder 5 → Wednesday + 5 = Monday. Always divide by 7 and use only the remainder.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: Repeating calendars
tips.body: A leap year's calendar repeats after 28 years (2020 → 2048). Ordinary years repeat after 6, 11 or 11 years depending on position in the leap cycle — if asked, the safe approach is to count odd days.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: Time rule
tips.body: A 4–5 question seating set is worth 4–5 marks but can swallow five minutes. On the first pass, skip it. Come back only if you have time left. Never let one arrangement puzzle cost you twenty easy questions at the back of the paper.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: Method — say the relationship out loud in one sentence
tips.body: "Pen is used to write, so knife is used to cut." Once you can state the relationship as a sentence, the answer is forced. If two options both fit, your sentence was too vague — make it more specific.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: Classification (odd one out)
tips.body: Look for the one category rule that covers three items and excludes one. Copper, Zinc, Aluminium are elements; Brass is an alloy. 17, 37, 47 are prime; 27 is not. Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri are rivers; Sundarbans is not.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: Mirror image (mirror held vertically, left–right flip)
tips.body: Letters that stay unchanged: A H I M O T U V W X Y — these are symmetric about a vertical axis. Memory: "A HIM O TUV WXY" — read it as a phrase.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: Water image (mirror held horizontally, top–bottom flip)
tips.body: Letters that stay unchanged: B C D E H I K O X — symmetric about a horizontal axis. Note H, I, O, X appear in both lists — they are symmetric both ways, and that is itself a common question.

tips.subject: Reasoning
tips.title: Painted cube formulas
tips.body: A cube painted on all sides and cut into n³ smaller cubes: 3 faces painted (corners) = 8 always · 2 faces (edges) = 12(n−2) · 1 face = 6(n−2)² · 0 faces = (n−2)³ For a cube cut into 64 pieces (n = 4): 8 corners, 12×2 = 24 edges, 6×4 = 24 one-face, 2³ = 8 unpainted. The four numbers must add to 64 — always check.

tips.subject: Telangana Movement
tips.title: Start here — the one idea the whole movement rests on
tips.body: Three grievances, repeated in every phase from 1952 to 2014. The movement's own slogan names them: "NEELLU — NIDHULU — NIYAMAKALU" = Waters — Funds — Appointments (jobs). Irrigation water going elsewhere, Telangana's surplus revenue being spent elsewhere, and outsiders taking local government jobs. Every agitation, committee and safeguard in these notes is a response to one of those three. If a question asks "why", the answer is one of these three words.

tips.subject: Telangana Movement
tips.title: Trick — Phase 1 in five numbers
tips.body: 19 – 30 – 38 – 46 – 48 → Mulki Rules, Andhra Mahasabha, Vande Mataram, Armed Struggle, Police Action. Say the five numbers aloud until they run together; then attach one word to each.

tips.subject: Telangana Movement
tips.title: Trick — the SRC point that gets asked
tips.body: The SRC did not recommend immediate merger; it recommended waiting until 1961. Merger happened anyway in 1956 on the strength of the Gentlemen's Agreement. "SRC said wait — they merged anyway — the agreement was broken — 1969 happened." That one sentence is the whole causal chain.

tips.subject: Telangana Movement
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: "69 = students; 2009 = leaders." The 1969 agitation was driven by students and collapsed when its leader joined the ruling party. The 2009–14 phase was driven by a political party plus a students' JAC and did not collapse. Examiners like the contrast.

tips.subject: Telangana Movement
tips.title: Trick — the two "371" facts people mix up
tips.body: Article 371-D = special provisions for Andhra Pradesh/Telangana (local-area recruitment, Administrative Tribunal), inserted by the 32nd Amendment, 1973. Do not confuse it with Article 370 (Jammu & Kashmir) or 371-A (Nagaland). "D for the Deccan."

tips.subject: Telangana Movement
tips.title: Trick — Phase 5 as a five-step ladder
tips.body: 2001 party → 2009 fast → 2010 committee → 2011 mass strike → 2013 decision → 2014 state Six steps, six numbers. Recite them in order every morning for a week and this entire phase becomes automatic. Note the pattern: party first, protest second, committee third, decision last — the same order as almost every successful statehood movement in India.

tips.subject: Telangana Movement
tips.title: Trick — three commissions, three initials
tips.body: F–J–G–S: Fazl Ali (1953), Jayabharat (1980s), Girglani (2001), Srikrishna (2010). Roughly one every twenty to thirty years — and the dates run in order, so the sequence itself is the memory aid.

tips.subject: Telangana GS
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Memory hook for the agitation years: 52 (Mulki) → 56 (merger) → 69 (Telangana) → 72 (Andhra) → 73 (Six-Point) → 2001 (TRS) → 2014 (state). Six numbers. Learn the sequence and most questions in this block answer themselves.

tips.subject: Telangana GS
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Note on schemes and current affairs: scheme names, amounts and beneficiary numbers change with governments and budgets. Learn the purpose of each scheme from these notes, and take the latest figures and any new schemes from a current-affairs compilation dated close to your exam.

tips.subject: Indian History
tips.title: Trick — the site table
tips.body: "Lothal = dockyard (L for Landing). Kalibangan = plough (K for Krishi/farming). Mohenjo-daro = Great Bath." Those three answers cover most IVC questions. Also remember: a Bronze Age civilisation, town planning on a grid, drainage system, and the script is still undeciphered.

tips.subject: Indian History
tips.title: Trick — Buddha's four places
tips.body: "L-B-S-K: Lumbini born, Bodh Gaya enlightened, Sarnath sermon, Kushinagar died." Birth to death in alphabetical-sounding order. Buddhist councils: Rajgriha → Vaishali → Pataliputra (Ashoka) → Kashmir (Kanishka).

tips.subject: Indian History
tips.title: Trick — the two Chinese travellers
tips.body: "Fa-Hien came for the Guptas, Hiuen Tsang came for Harsha." Both start with H going together — Hiuen with Harsha. That pairing alone settles a very common question.

tips.subject: Indian History
tips.title: Trick — the five dynasties
tips.body: "Slave Kings Try Some Luck" = Slave, Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi. Never mix the order; the dates always rise: 1206 → 1290 → 1320 → 1414 → 1451.

tips.subject: Indian History
tips.title: Trick — Mughal order
tips.body: "BHAJSA" = Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb. Six emperors, one word. And the three Panipats: 1526 – 1556 – 1761 (Babur, Akbar, Marathas vs Abdali).

tips.subject: Indian History
tips.title: Trick — Governors-General by their one famous act
tips.body: Hastings = first · Cornwallis = Permanent Settlement · Bentinck = Sati abolished · Dalhousie = Railways & Doctrine of Lapse · Canning = first Viceroy · Ripon = local self-government · Curzon = Partition of Bengal · Mountbatten = last Viceroy One name, one act. Learn the pairs, not the biographies.

tips.subject: Indian History
tips.title: Trick — the freedom struggle in eight numbers
tips.body: 1857 → 1885 → 1905 → 1919 → 1920 → 1930 → 1942 → 1947 Revolt · Congress · Partition of Bengal · Jallianwala · Non-Cooperation · Dandi · Quit India · Freedom. Recite these eight aloud daily. Almost every modern-history question sits on or between two of them — even when you don't know the answer, the ladder tells you which decade is plausible and kills two options.

tips.subject: Indian History
tips.title: Trick — Gandhi's movements in order
tips.body: "Champaran → Kheda → Ahmedabad → Non-Cooperation → Dandi → Quit India" = C-K-A-N-D-Q. The first three are the 1917–18 satyagrahas; then one big movement per decade: 1920, 1930, 1942 — a neat twelve-year, twelve-year rhythm.

tips.subject: Geography
tips.title: Trick — the 8 states on the Tropic of Cancer, west to east
tips.body: Gujarat → Rajasthan → Madhya Pradesh → Chhattisgarh → Jharkhand → West Bengal → Tripura → Mizoram "Gujarat Rajasthan Ma Chhattisgarh Jharkhand West Tripura Mizoram" = G R M C J W T M Sentence version: "Great Rulers May Choose Jackfruit With Tasty Mango."

tips.subject: Geography
tips.title: Trick — border length order
tips.body: "BC PNM BA" → Bangladesh, China, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan, Afghanistan. And the lines: "Ra-Pa (Radcliffe–Pakistan), Mac-Chi (McMahon–China), Du-Af (Durand–Afghanistan)".

tips.subject: Geography
tips.title: Trick — Himalayan ranges, north to south
tips.body: "HHS = Himadri, Himachal, Shivalik" — height decreases as you move south, and so does the name's importance. Greater → Lesser → Outer.

tips.subject: Geography
tips.title: Trick — the five Punjab rivers
tips.body: "J C R B S" → Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej. Sentence: "Just Come Right Back Soon."

tips.subject: Geography
tips.title: Trick — which rivers flow WEST?
tips.body: Only a handful: Narmada, Tapti, Mahi, Sabarmati, Luni, Periyar. Everything else on the peninsula flows east into the Bay of Bengal. "NT MSLP go West" — and remember Narmada and Tapti flow in rift valleys, which is why they don't form deltas — they form estuaries.

tips.subject: Geography
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: "Black soil = Black cotton soil". And "Red = iRon". Those two answers alone cover most soil questions.

tips.subject: Geography
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: "Kharif comes with the Kharab weather (monsoon rain) — Rice. Rabi is the Rabi-winter crop — Wheat." If you remember only two words: Kharif = Rice, Rabi = Wheat. Most questions are answered by that pair.

tips.subject: Geography
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: Odisha is the answer to more mineral questions than any other state — iron, bauxite, manganese, chromite, coal. If you must guess a mineral state, guess Odisha or Jharkhand.

tips.subject: Geography
tips.title: Trick — layers of the atmosphere, bottom to top
tips.body: Troposphere → Stratosphere → Mesosphere → Thermosphere → Exosphere "The Strong Man Threw Everything" Weather happens in the troposphere; the ozone layer is in the stratosphere.

tips.subject: Geography
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Equator 0° · Tropic of Cancer 23½° N · Tropic of Capricorn 23½° S · Arctic Circle 66½° N · Antarctic Circle 66½° S · Prime Meridian 0° through Greenwich · International Date Line ≈ 180°. "Cancer is up North (C for Cancer, N for North)." Latitudes run east–west and measure distance north–south; longitudes are the opposite.

tips.subject: Polity
tips.title: Trick — the three dates people confuse
tips.body: 1946 formed → 1949 adopted (26 Nov) → 1950 enforced (26 Jan). Say it as "formed, adopted, enforced". November is adoption; January is enforcement.

tips.subject: Polity
tips.title: Trick — the four you must never mix up
tips.body: USA → Rights · Ireland → Directives · USSR → Duties · UK → Parliament Sentence: "America gives Rights, Ireland gives Directions, Russia gives Duties, Britain gives the Parliament." Four countries, four Ds/Rs — this single line answers most borrowed-features questions.

tips.subject: Polity
tips.title: Two tricks for the Preamble
tips.body: 1. The four objectives: "J-L-E-F" = Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity — remember "JLEF" in that order; questions often test the order. 2. The words added later: Socialist, Secular and Integrity were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976). "S-S-I came in '76". The 42nd is the only amendment that ever changed the Preamble.

tips.subject: Polity
tips.title: Trick — Parts III and IV
tips.body: "Rights come Three, Directives come Four, Duties are Four-A." III → Rights, IV → Directives, IV-A → Duties. In numerical order, and that is exactly how they were added historically (Duties last, in 1976).

tips.subject: Polity
tips.title: Trick — the five schedules that are actually asked
tips.body: 7 = three Lists · 8 = 22 Languages · 10 = Defection · 11 = Panchayat · 12 = Municipality Note the neat pattern at the end: 11 is villages, 12 is towns — the bigger number is the bigger settlement. And "Seventh has the Seven-day argument between Centre and State" (the three Lists).

tips.subject: Polity
tips.title: Trick — six rights in order
tips.body: E–F–E–R–C–C = Equality, Freedom, against Exploitation, Religion, Cultural & Educational, Constitutional Remedies. Sentence: "Every Friend Enjoys Real Cultural Company." Six rights — the Right to Property was removed (44th Amendment, 1978) and is now only a legal right under Article 300A.

tips.subject: Polity
tips.title: Shortcut
tips.body: Speech and expression · Assemble peacefully · Form associations · Move freely · Reside and settle · Practise any profession. "SAFMRP" — Speech, Assembly, Association, Movement, Residence, Profession. The right to property was the seventh and was deleted.

tips.subject: Polity
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: "He Must Please Cricket Quickly" = Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo Warranto. And for the pair people confuse: Prohibition comes before, Certiorari comes after — "P before C", alphabetical order matches the time order.

tips.subject: Polity
tips.title: Trick — Rights vs Directives vs Duties
tips.body: Rights = enforceable · Directives = not enforceable · Duties = not enforceable. Only Fundamental Rights can take you to court. "Only Rights are Right-able in court."

tips.subject: Polity
tips.title: Trick — the age ladder
tips.body: 25 – 30 – 35 → Lok Sabha 25, Rajya Sabha 30, President/VP/Governor 35. Rises in steps of five, in order of seniority. Easiest three marks in polity.

tips.subject: Polity
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: "Money starts in the Lok Sabha and money ends in the Lok Sabha." The Rajya Sabha has no real power over money — that single idea answers most Money Bill questions.

tips.subject: Polity
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: 352 → 356 → 360 = Nation → State → Finance. The numbers rise as the scope narrows: whole nation first, then a state, then money. And the last one, 360, has never happened — a fact that is itself a common question.

tips.subject: Polity
tips.title: Trick — the amendments most often asked
tips.body: 42 adds, 44 removes — the 42nd added Duties and Preamble words; the 44th removed the Right to Property. Then "73 = village, 74 = town" (same odd/even logic as Schedules 11 and 12), and "86 = education".

tips.subject: Economy & GK
tips.title: Trick — the two facts examiners ask about sectors
tips.body: In India the tertiary (service) sector contributes the largest share of GDP, but the primary sector employs the largest number of people. Those two facts look contradictory, which is exactly why they are asked. "Services earn the most; agriculture feeds the most families."

tips.subject: Economy & GK
tips.title: Trick — GDP vs GNP
tips.body: "D = Domestic (inside the borders). N = National (our people, wherever they are)." A Japanese factory in India counts in India's GDP; an Indian working abroad counts in India's GNP. In India, GDP is estimated by the National Statistical Office (NSO).

tips.subject: Economy & GK
tips.title: Trick — the two plans always asked
tips.body: "First = Farming. Second = Steel (heavy industry, Mahalanobis)." If a question names the Mahalanobis model, the answer is the Second Plan. If it names Harrod–Domar or agriculture, it is the First.

tips.subject: Economy & GK
tips.title: Two tricks that settle every monetary-policy question
tips.body: 1. Repo vs reverse repo: "REPO — RBI lends. REVERSE — the reverse, RBI borrows." 2. CRR vs SLR: "CRR — Cash goes to the RBI. SLR — Stays with the Lender (the bank itself)." And the direction is always the same: every one of these tools, when raised, reduces money supply and fights inflation. If a question asks "to control inflation the RBI will…", the answer is increase — whichever tool is named.

tips.subject: Economy & GK
tips.title: Trick — who regulates what
tips.body: "RBI → banks and money · SEBI → share market · IRDAI → insurance · PFRDA → pensions · NABARD → rural/agricultural credit · SIDBI → small industries · EXIM Bank → foreign trade." One line, five marks.

tips.subject: Economy & GK
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: "Inflation is a friend to the borrower and an enemy to the saver." If the question asks who is hurt most by inflation, the answer is always the person on a fixed income.

tips.subject: Economy & GK
tips.title: Trick — direct or indirect?
tips.body: "If you can pass the bill to someone else, it's INdirect." You cannot pass on your income tax — direct. The shopkeeper passes GST to you — indirect. Also remember: GST is one tax, one nation, one market, and it is indirect.

tips.subject: Economy & GK
tips.title: Trick — the revolutions, by colour logic
tips.body: Almost every colour looks like the product: White = MILK · Blue = water → FISH · Yellow = mustard oil → OILSEEDS · Pink = prawn · Black = crude oil · Silver = eggshell · Golden = honey/fruit · Red = meat and tomato · Round = potato. Only Green (food grains) and Grey (fertilizer) need real memorising. Learn the four big ones cold — Green–grain, White–milk, Blue–fish, Yellow–oilseed — as they cover most questions.

tips.subject: Economy & GK
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: "1991 = LPG" — the same three letters as cooking gas, and the same year the economy opened up. The two names attached to it are Narasimha Rao and Manmohan Singh.

tips.subject: Economy & GK
tips.title: Trick — HDI's three legs
tips.body: "Live long, learn well, earn enough" = life expectancy, education, income. And remember the publisher is the UNDP, not the World Bank — the swap is a standard trap.

tips.subject: Economy & GK
tips.title: Trick — World Bank vs IMF
tips.body: "World Bank builds (long-term projects). IMF bails out (short-term crises)." Both were created at the Bretton Woods conference of 1944 and both sit in Washington DC. WTO and ILO are in Geneva; UN and UNDP in New York.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — the "-est" list, always asked in one form or another
tips.body: Largest gland = liver · Largest organ = skin · Largest cell = ovum · Longest cell = nerve cell · Smallest bone = stapes (in the ear) · Longest bone = femur (thigh) · Largest bone = femur · Strongest muscle = jaw muscle · Largest artery = aorta · Smallest bone and smallest muscle are both in the ear. Memory: "Liver is the biggest gland, Skin is the biggest organ, Stapes is the smallest bone."

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: "Pepsin–Protein, Lipase–Lipid (fat), Amylase–Amylum (starch)" — each enzyme starts with the same sound as what it digests.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — donor vs recipient
tips.body: "O gives to all (O = Owes everyone). AB takes from all (AB = All Blood)."

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: Pancreas is the only organ that is both a gland (insulin) and a digestive organ (enzymes). That dual role is itself a favourite question.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Three tricks that cover most vitamin questions
tips.body: 1. Fat-soluble vitamins are A D E K — remember the word "ADEK". Everything else (B group and C) is water-soluble. 2. "K = Klotting" — vitamin K is for blood clotting. 3. "D from the Daylight, C from Citrus, A for the eyes (A = eyesight in the dArk)".

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — the mosquito table (asked almost every year)
tips.body: MosquitoDisease it carries Anopheles (female)Malaria AedesDengue, chikungunya, zika, yellow fever CulexFilariasis, Japanese encephalitis "A-A-C = Anopheles–Malaria, Aedes–Dengue, Culex–Filaria" — alphabetical order of the mosquito matches alphabetical order of the disease: Anopheles–Malaria, Aedes–Dengue, Culex–Filaria.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — which organ does each disease attack?
tips.body: TB → lungs · Jaundice/hepatitis → liver · Cataract and glaucoma → eye · Arthritis → joints · Diabetes → pancreas · Goitre → thyroid · Anaemia → blood · Pyorrhoea → gums · Asthma → bronchi/lungs.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Photosynthesis — memorise this one line
tips.body: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O --(sunlight, chlorophyll)--> C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ Happens in the chloroplast, which contains the green pigment chlorophyll (chlorophyll contains magnesium). Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: "Mighty Mitochondria make Money (energy). Lousy Lysosome is the suicide bag. Ribosome = pRotein."

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — the seven base units
tips.body: "Mary Kept Silent About Kevin's Momentary Cough" → Metre, Kilogram, Second, Ampere, Kelvin, Mole, Candela. Everything else (newton, joule, watt, pascal, volt, ohm…) is a derived unit — a favourite trap question.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: Most instrument names tell you the answer if you read them: "-meter" = measures. Hygro = moisture, Pyro = fire/heat, Anemo = wind, Alti = height, Tacho = speed of rotation, Lacto = milk, Hydro = water. Learn the prefix, not the whole word.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — scalar or vector?
tips.body: Scalars (magnitude only): distance, speed, mass, time, energy, work, power, temperature, density. Vectors (magnitude + direction): displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, momentum, weight. "If you can point in its direction, it is a vector." Note that weight is a vector but mass is a scalar.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: "Mass is what you ARE; weight is what the planet DOES to you." Any question that says "on the Moon", the answer is almost always about weight becoming 1/6 while mass stays the same.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — energy conversions asked in exams
tips.body: Electric bulb: electrical → light + heat · Loudspeaker: electrical → sound · Microphone: sound → electrical · Battery: chemical → electrical · Dynamo/generator: mechanical → electrical · Electric motor: electrical → mechanical · Solar cell: light → electrical. Motor and generator are exact opposites — remember one and you know the other.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — pressure and area
tips.body: Same force, smaller area → greater pressure. That is why a sharp knife cuts better, a nail has a pointed tip, and why camels have broad feet and tractors have wide tyres (large area → less pressure → they don't sink).

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — the anomalous expansion of water
tips.body: Water contracts from 0 °C to 4 °C and expands after that, so it is densest at 4 °C. This is why ice floats and why fish survive under a frozen lake — the water at the bottom stays at 4 °C. This single fact appears again and again.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: "Sound needs a medium; light does not." Any question about the Moon, space or vacuum — sound fails, light succeeds. And "20 to 20,000" is the human hearing range; below is infra, above is ultra.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — mirrors
tips.body: "CoNcave = CoNverges and is used Close up (shaving, dentist). ConVex = diVerges and gives a Vast View (rear-view mirror)."

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — the eye defects, in one line
tips.body: "MY-opia takes a MINUS (concave) lens; HYPER-metropia takes a PLUS (convex) lens." Concave lenses have negative power, convex positive. Lens power is measured in dioptres (D) = 1 ÷ focal length in metres.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — the Ohm's law triangle
tips.body: Write V on top with I and R below. Cover the one you want: cover V → I × R; cover I → V/R; cover R → V/I. Never mis-rearrange again.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — fission vs fusion
tips.body: "FISSion = SPLITting (both have an S sound at the break). FUSion = FUSing together." The Sun runs on fusion; a nuclear power plant runs on fission.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — the sublimation list
tips.body: "CANDI = Camphor, Ammonium chloride, Naphthalene, Dry ice, Iodine." Almost every sublimation question uses one of these five.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: "IsoTOPes — same TOP (top of the symbol is the atomic number, i.e. same element). IsoBARs — same BAR of mass." Carbon-14 dating uses an isotope of carbon.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Three tricks for the groups
tips.body: Alkali metals: "Li Na Ki Rab Se Fariyad" → Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr. Noble gases: "He Never Argued, Krishna Xeroxed Regularly" → He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn. Halogens: "F Cl Br I At" — "Fluorine Clears Bright Iron At once." Remember also that halogens are the salt formers — that is literally what the word means.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: The trap is always the same: symbols that do not match the English name. If the question shows an element whose symbol looks unrelated, it is from this list. "Gold = Au (Aurum), Silver = Ag (Argentum), Iron = Fe (Ferrum), Lead = Pb (Plumbum)." Say those four aloud until automatic.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — the "soda" family
tips.body: All three are sodium compounds, and the name tells you which: BAKING soda = biCARBonate (NaHCO₃) · WASHING soda = CARBonate (Na₂CO₃) · CAUSTIC soda = hydrOXIDE (NaOH) And the vitriols are all sulphates: blue = copper, green = ferrous, oil of = sulphuric acid.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick
tips.body: "Acid is Below 7, Base is Above 7" — and alphabetically Acid comes before Base, just as its number is smaller. For the sting: ant and bee = FORMIC (think "formica", the ant genus) — rubbing baking soda on it neutralises the acid.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — the two everyone confuses
tips.body: "BraSS has Zinc — Bronze has TiN." Say it as "Brass–Zinc, Bronze–Tin"; both other letters (S and N) hint at the partner. And German silver contains no silver at all — that itself is the question.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — air composition
tips.body: Nitrogen 78% · Oxygen 21% · Argon ~0.9% · Carbon dioxide ~0.03%. Remember "78-21" as a pair. And the two "balloon" gases differ: hydrogen is lighter but dangerous; helium is safe, which is why airships use helium.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — diamond vs graphite
tips.body: Both are pure carbon, yet opposite in every way: "Diamond is hard and does NOT conduct; graphite is soft and DOES conduct." The reason is the arrangement of atoms — that "same element, different properties" idea is the exam's favourite allotrope question.

tips.subject: General Science
tips.title: Trick — the three big pollution problems
tips.body: "CO₂ warms · CFC thins the ozone · SO₂ makes acid rain." Three gases, three distinct effects. Exams routinely try to swap them.
